target_moa.text: Spinosad is an insecticide/pediculicide that causes neuronal excitation in insects by altering the function of nicotinic and gamma butyric acid-gated ion channels, producing prolonged over-excitation; after hyperexcitation, lice become paralyzed and die.

citations.quote: Spinosad causes neuronal excitation in insects. After periods of hyperexcitation, lice become paralyzed and die.

Spinosad is an insecticide that works by causing paralysis of insects by altering the function of nicotinic and gamma butyric acid-gated ion channels resulting in prolonged over-excitation of the insect's nervous system.

modality.text: Small molecule (spinosad, a fermentation-derived insecticide composed of spinosyns A and D), new molecular entity

citations.quote: Spinosad is a new molecular entity, derived from the fermentation of a soil actinomycete bacterium, *Saccharopolyspora spinosa*.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse events (>1%) were application site erythema (3% spinosad vs 7% permethrin) and ocular erythema (2% vs 3%); application site irritation occurred in 1% (vs 2%). Less common reactions (<1% but >0.1%) included application site dryness, exfoliation, alopecia, and dry skin.

vote.text: No Advisory Committee was convened; NDA 22-408 was not presented to the Dermatology and Ophthalmology Drugs Advisory Committee because systemic exposure was below the level of detection and no safety signals or novel issues were identified.

citations.quote: No Advisory Committee was convened in response to this application.

NDA 22-408 was not presented to the Dermatology and Ophthalmology Drugs Advisory Committee because the systemic exposure to spinosad, as far as it was studied, was documented to be below the level of detection, and no concerning safety signals were identified during the development program.

detail.text: Not a first-cycle approval; the Division issued a Complete Response Letter on November 18, 2009 on the original NDA, and the application was approved after the applicant's complete response submitted July 23, 2010.

citations.quote: After review of the original NDA by the various disciplines, the action taken was a Complete Response on November 18, 2009. The reasons for this action included the following:
On July 23, 2010 the applicant submitted a "complete response to FDA's Complete Response Letter dated November 18, 2009," containing the following:

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated January 21, 2009, received January 22, 2009, submitted pursuant to section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Natroba (spinosad) Topical Suspension, 0.9%.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study under PREA (#1711): a pharmacokinetic and safety study in pediatric patients ages 6 months to 4 years with active head lice infestation, conducted under maximum use conditions with a minimum of 24 evaluable patients undergoing PK sampling and local/systemic safety assessments.

citations.quote: 1711 A pharmacokinetic and safety study in pediatric patients ages 6 months to 4 years of age with active head lice infestation. This study should be conducted under maximum use conditions and include a minimum of 24 evaluable patients who will undergo pharmacokinetic sampling and assessments of local and systemic safety at appropriate time points.
A Complete Response Letter was issued November 18, 2009.

basis.text: FDA concluded the product appeared to contain two active ingredients (spinosad and benzyl alcohol), because a product containing 5% benzyl alcohol had recently been approved as an active ingredient for head lice; the applicant was asked to provide information to support benzyl alcohol as an inactive ingredient (plus PK and CMC items).

citations.quote: However, we have recently approved a product containing benzyl alcohol (present at 5%) as an active ingredient for the treatment of head lice. This would indicate that your product contains two active ingredients: spinosad and benzyl alcohol (b) (4).

basis.text: The application was granted a standard review (Priority Designation: Standard).

citations.quote: NDA 022408 was originally submitted on January 21, 2009, received on January 22, 2009, and granted a standard review.

summary.text: NATROBA (spinosad), a new molecular entity, was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA and granted standard review; it was not referred to an advisory committee. The original NDA received a Complete Response Letter on November 18, 2009 (over whether benzyl alcohol was a second active ingredient), and was approved following the applicant's complete response, with a deferred PREA pediatric PK/safety study as a postmarketing requirement.
